hypothesis: Per the curated popularity-bias survey note (option (a): reweight training examples inversely to item popularity), reweight each BPR training pair by `pop_video^(-pop_alpha)` (mean-normalized so `pop_alpha=0` exactly reproduces the current best) so that positives on ultra-popular videos contribute less gradient than positives on long-tail videos — this is a genuinely untried lever (all prior attempts were capacity/architecture/temporal-reweighting, never popularity-aware reweighting) and directly targets the EDA's documented Gini=0.79 popularity skew, which the `pop`-only baseline already shows explains a large share of achievable score.
reflection: The recency-reweighting experiment gave numerically identical results to baseline (decay=0 reproduced exactly, and nonzero decays all underperformed), so temporal drift within the training window just isn't the lever — the FM+BPR architecture at k=16 has now plateaued across five straight rejections spanning capacity (k, DeepFM, FwFM), regularization (weight decay), and reweighting (recency, DNS) changes. Given the plateau warning I considered a research question, but I already have a concrete, literature-grounded, genuinely untried lever in hand (popularity_debiasing via inverse-popularity example reweighting) that doesn't need IPS/randomized-exposure data (which we've confirmed is unavailable) — so I'll spend this turn testing that mechanism directly rather than researching further.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more than nDCG@5, since debiasing popularity specifically improves within-user discrimination between items of differing true relevance regardless of raw popularity — which is exactly what GAUC (an average of per-user pairwise AUCs) measures — whereas nDCG@5's top-5 cutoff is more directly dominated by whichever items are truly most relevant to that user, a less popularity-confounded quantity to begin with.
